page: Microsoft Azure M16ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. It allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores using symmetric multithreading, backed by 38 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector instructions. Memory provisioning is the defining characteristic of this instance, delivering 438.0 GB of system RAM, translating to an extensive 27.34 GB of memory per vCPU. Local storage is provided via an integrated 550 GB solid-state drive, while graphics processing units are absent.

Performance benchmarks reflect the architectural intent of the M-series platform, balancing massive memory capacity with standard compute throughput. In synthetic processor workloads, single-threaded metrics such as Geekbench single-core (878.0) and single-core stress-ng (1038.48) place in the lower tier, whereas multi-core execution scales solidly into average ranges with a PassMark CPU score of 11764.97 and Geekbench multi-core score of 5698.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 73.69 GB/sec alongside 35.88 GB/sec write bandwidth, enabling the instance to achieve 10.46 million Redis SET operations per second and stable static throughput.

Cost efficiency is centered entirely around RAM density rather than pure processing speed. Deploying 16 vCPUs alongside 438 GB of RAM allows organizations to minimize per-core licensing expenses while hosting massive working datasets. While unsuitable for compute-bound single-threaded applications or large language model inference (yielding only 7.1 tokens/sec on 7B parameter models), the Azure M16ms offers an optimal resource envelope for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational database systems, and heavy in-memory data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M16ms is a memory-optimized instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. Tailored for memory-intensive enterprise environments, the platform features 438.0 GB of RAM, equating to 27.34 GB per core, complemented by a local 550 GB SSD for temporary storage. In benchmark evaluations, multi-threaded CPU throughput and memory bandwidth deliver steady midrange scores, demonstrated by 10.46 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark CPU rating of 11764.97. Single-threaded metrics, including compression and decompression tasks, reflect lower relative performance. The resource profile makes this instance qualitatively cost-effective for consolidating high-memory workloads under moderate core counts, serving applications such as large relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and enterprise data analytics.
